case_title: Santosh @ Rajesh @ Gopal v. State of Madhya Pradesh
statutory_provisions: IPC s.302, s.34; Arms Act s.25(1-B)(A)
neutral_facts: The prosecution alleged that on 13.11.2011, at 9:30 p.m., the victim, Narayan Singh, was shot dead at his home in Village Binjana, District Dewas, Madhya Pradesh. The victim's mother, Rachna Bai, testified that she and the victim were sleeping when someone called out the victim's name, prompting him to open the door. A gunshot was heard, and shortly after, a second gunshot struck the victim in the chest, causing him to fall. Rachna Bai saw her daughter-in-law and the victim's son standing on the opposite side of the house and two individuals with their faces covered fleeing the scene on a motorcycle. The prosecution's primary evidence against the appellant was the recovery of a pistol from him and a ballistic report confirming that the bullet recovered from the victim's body was fired from the recovered pistol. There were no eyewitnesses to the crime, and the case against the appellant rested entirely on circumstantial evidence.
